neighbours.label: the unit or suffix token attached directly to a decimal number that modifies a noun ('a 1.5 [month] rebate', '5.8[G] transmitter', '2.5 [axis] machining')
fire: The landlord offered every tenant a 1.5 month discount on next year's rent.
Most older phones still shipped with a 3.5mm headphone socket on the top edge.
The hotel dropped to a 4.5 star rating after the renovation was delayed.
Our router broadcasts on the 2.4G band as well as the faster one.
The club organised a 2.5 mile walk around the reservoir for beginners.
He screwed a sheet of 0.5 inch plywood over the broken window.
The storm caused a 1.5 hour delay at the ferry terminal this morning.
She signed a 2.5 year contract with the club before the season began.
quiet: The landlord offered every tenant a two month discount on next year's rent.
Most older phones still shipped with a round headphone socket on the top edge.
The hotel dropped to a four star rating after the renovation was delayed.
Our router broadcasts on the older band as well as the faster one.
The club organised a three mile walk around the reservoir for beginners.
He screwed a sheet of half inch plywood over the broken window.
The storm caused an hour long delay at the ferry terminal this morning.
The index closed at 2.5 and the yield slipped back to 1.5 by Friday.

notes: Card: peaks on ' month', 'G', ' axis', 'a', ' day', 'mm', ' yards', ' stars', each right after a decimal like 1.5 or 2.5. Probes: '2.5 day weekend' 1.13 and '2.4G' 0.83, but '3.5 miles' used as a plain measure only 0.17 and 'three day weekend' 0.04, so the test uses the decimal+unit as a modifier. The + pole is the last digit of a decimal price, so both poles read decimals.
